knowledge:
- key_parameters: x / train.dat=matrix of training gene expression data (genes as columns, samples as rows) ;; surv.time / surv.time.train=vector of survival times for the training set ;; cens.vec / cens.vec.train=vector of censoring status for the training set (0 = censored, 1 = uncensored) ;; nbest=number of models to keep for each BMA iteration ;; p=number of top univariate sorted genes to be used in the iterative calls to the bic.surv algorithm ;; cutPoint=percentage cutoff for separating the high-risk group from the low-risk group ;; diseaseType=disease type string used for naming cross-validation output files ;; noRuns=number of cross-validation runs ;; noFolds=number of cross-validation folds
- alternatives: Traditional BMA (via bic.surv in the BMA package) which is inefficient for datasets with more than 30 variables ;; Cox Proportional Hazards Model alone, which is used as a univariate pre-ranking step but ignores model uncertainty and gene-gene interactions
- when_to_use: When performing survival analysis on high-dimensional transcriptomics (microarray) data to identify a small subset of predictive genes and classify patients into risk groups while accounting for model uncertainty
- pitfalls: If all test samples are assigned to a single risk group or all samples are in the same censor category, the algorithm returns success = FALSE ;; The traditional BMA algorithm is inefficient for >30 variables, so the sliding window size (maxNvar) is typically limited to 25 or 30 ;; Using too small a value for p (number of top genes) or nbest might yield less significant results

workflows.name: step_by_step_survival_analysis
workflows.intent: Train the iterative BMA model step-by-step, predict risk scores for test samples, assign them to risk categories, evaluate survival differences, and visualize the selected models.
input: trainData (matrix of training gene expression data)
testData (matrix of test gene expression data)
workflows.stages: 1. Load training data and run iterateBMAsurv.train.wrapper to select relevant genes ;; 2. Extract the bic.surv object and identify top genes with posterior probability > 0 ;; 3. Load test data and subset it to the selected top genes ;; 4. Predict risk scores for test and training samples using predictBicSurv ;; 5. Assign test samples to risk categories using predictiveAssessCategory ;; 6. Perform survival difference analysis using survdiff ;; 7. Visualize selected genes and models using imageplot.iterate.bma.surv
workflows.code:
library(BMA)
library(iterativeBMAsurv)
data(trainData)
data(trainSurv)
data(trainCens)
ret.list <- iterateBMAsurv.train.wrapper (x=trainData, surv.time=trainSurv, cens.vec=trainCens, nbest=5)
ret.bic.surv <- ret.list$obj
gene.names <- ret.list$curr.names
top.gene.names <- gene.names[ret.bic.surv$probne0 > 0]
top.gene.names
ret.bic.surv$postprob
data(testData)
data(testSurv)
data(testCens)
curr.test.dat <- testData[, top.gene.names]
y.pred.test <- apply (curr.test.dat, 1, predictBicSurv, postprob.vec=ret.bic.surv$postprob, mle.mat=ret.bic.surv$mle)
y.pred.train <- apply (trainData[, top.gene.names], 1, predictBicSurv, postprob.vec=ret.bic.surv$postprob, mle.mat=ret.bic.surv$mle)
ret.table <- predictiveAssessCategory (y.pred.test, y.pred.train, testCens, cutPoint=50) 
risk.vector <- ret.table$groups
risk.table <- ret.table$assign.risk
risk.table
mySurv.obj <- Surv(testSurv, testCens)
stats <- survdiff(mySurv.obj ~ unlist(risk.vector))
stats
imageplot.iterate.bma.surv (ret.bic.surv)

workflows.name: automated_survival_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform gene selection, model training, risk prediction, and risk group assessment in a single automated function call.
input: trainData (matrix of training gene expression data)
testData (matrix of test gene expression data)
workflows.stages: 1. Run iterateBMAsurv.train.predict.assess to perform the entire pipeline ;; 2. Extract statistics and evaluation metrics from the returned object
workflows.code:
library(BMA)
library(iterativeBMAsurv)
data(trainData)
data(trainSurv)
data(trainCens)
data(testData)
data(testSurv)
data(testCens)
ret.bma <- iterateBMAsurv.train.predict.assess (train.dat=trainData, test.dat=testData, surv.time.train=trainSurv, surv.time.test=testSurv, cens.vec.train=trainCens, cens.vec.test=testCens, p=10, nbest=5)
number.genes <- ret.bma$nvar
number.models <- ret.bma$nmodel
evaluate.success <- ret.bma$statistics
evaluate.success

workflows.name: cross_validation
workflows.intent: Perform k-run n-fold cross-validation on the training set to evaluate model performance and optimize parameters.
input: trainData (matrix of training gene expression data)
workflows.stages: 1. Run crossVal with specified folds, runs, and parameters to evaluate the model and write results to files
workflows.code:
library(BMA)
library(iterativeBMAsurv)
data(trainData)
data(trainSurv)
data(trainCens)
cv <- crossVal (exset=trainData, survTime=trainSurv, censor=trainCens, diseaseType="DLBCL", noRuns=1, noFolds=2, p=10, nbest=5)
